acceptance_checks.description: Total events processed for ds=2026-01-15 equals 272 (240 from the SQS queue, 32 from DynamoDB), recomputed by querying the deployed silver table, not read from a log line.

Daily aggregates recomputed from ow_tp.gold.analytics_daily_summary equal the baseline manifest values exactly: active_users=12, active_documents=25, active_files=9, total_events=272, plus every per-action count and bytes_uploaded.

The user-resolution precedence of the legacy resolver is preserved: first non-empty of ownerId, editedBy, authorId, deletedBy, userId wins; events with none of those fields resolve to the literal 'unknown'. Per-user aggregates must match the baseline top_users artifact as a set of (user_id, counts) tuples.
DynamoDB date filtering keeps the same boundary semantics as begins_with(event_date, '2026-01-15'): the 16 seeded adjacent-day events (2026-01-14 and 2026-01-16) are excluded from ds=2026-01-15.

The three gold artifacts the downstream cron-activity unit consumes (daily summary row, top_users, hourly breakdown) exist for ds=2026-01-15 with the same logical content as the baseline gzip artifacts; comparison is over decoded content, not gzip bytes.

Rerunning the job for the same ds is idempotent: the gold row count for ds=2026-01-15 stays at one row per date (legacy did ON CONFLICT (report_date) DO UPDATE) and all recomputed values are unchanged.
The legacy report's volatile generated_at field is excluded from comparison; every other field of reports/analytics/daily/2026-01-15/report.json is reproduced.

encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Event payload text is carried through verbatim; multi-byte content (e.g. the seeded 'Réunion café ☕' titles and 'Δelta' names) must survive ingestion, aggregation and artifact emission without escaping, transliteration, or replacement characters.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: A message body that is not decodable UTF-8 is treated as a malformed record (see malformed_record_policy), never silently coerced with replacement characters.

malformed_record_policy.details: Legacy silently swallowed unparseable SQS bodies in a bare except and left them in the queue's delete batch path unaccounted for. The migrated unit must tolerate them but attribute them: all 8 seeded malformed bodies land in ow_tp.bronze.cronbox_events_rejected with a reason, and the rejected count is asserted as 8. Events carrying none of the five user-id fields keep the legacy attribution to the literal 'unknown' (22 seeded events) rather than being dropped.

empty_input_semantics.details: Legacy printed a warning and exited 0 without writing any S3 artifact or Postgres row when zero events were found. The migrated job must likewise leave prior outputs untouched and write nothing for the date — it must not write an all-zero gold row, which would corrupt the cron-activity 30-day lookback.

planted_anomalies.description: 8 non-JSON SQS message bodies in the run-date queue.
22 events carrying none of ownerId/editedBy/authorId/deletedBy/userId, which must aggregate under the literal user id 'unknown'.
16 DynamoDB events dated 2026-01-14 and 2026-01-16 that must be excluded from the 2026-01-15 batch.
Multi-byte titles and names ('Réunion café ☕', 'Δelta') that must survive byte-transparently into the gold artifacts.
The legacy upsert stamps analytics_daily_summary.updated_at with database NOW(), so it is not reproducible and is excluded from value comparison.
planted_anomalies.reason: The value is produced by the database clock inside immutable legacy SQL; it carries no business meaning and cannot be reconciled deterministically. Business columns are compared in full.

planted_anomalies.description: reports/analytics/daily/<ds>/report.json carries a generated_at from datetime.now(), which leaks fractional seconds even under the frozen libfaketime clock.
planted_anomalies.reason: Declared volatile in the baseline capture; the canonical checksum is computed with the field removed and the observed value is recorded as non-comparable evidence.
